title: 2026 HSE end-status and main-scheme conversion QA

sources.publisher: Environment Agency and Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme for hospital or small emitters: how to comply

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: UK ETS: Hospital and Small Emitter status

facts.source_fact: A small-emitter HSE can receive a conversion notice if reportable emissions exceed 24,999 tCO2e in 2026, 2027 or 2028.
A hospital-service HSE can receive a conversion notice if it stops primarily providing hospital services unless it qualifies as a small emitter instead.
A conversion notice requires compliance with GHGE permit conditions from 1 January of the scheme year following the notice year.
The operator must apply to vary the monitoring plan to meet GHGE permit requirements.
The regulator converts the HSE permit into a GHGE permit.
HSE permits for operators not qualifying in 2026–2030 after being HSE in 2021–2025 were converted effective 1 January 2026.
An HSE cannot voluntarily cease HSE status during an allocation period.
When HSE status ends, the operator enters the UK ETS main scheme in the following scheme year.
Main-scheme entry requires compliance with main UK ETS rules and a registry account.
Unpaid penalties and further sanctions from the HSE period remain liabilities after main-scheme entry.
